tickets.title: Initialize private repository and protected main
tickets.story: As an engineer, I can propose isolated changes with mandatory review.
acceptance: Repository has README, license decision, ignore rules and no live secrets.
Main requires passing CI and one independent review; force push and deletion are disabled.
An initial PR proves branch protections and records the tested commit.

tickets.title: Install and verify three agent workflows
tickets.story: As an engineer, I can use Claude Code, Cursor and Codex against one contract.
acceptance: CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md and current Cursor .mdc rules are loaded.
Each agent states the headless product invariant and runtime-role restriction.
An isolated worktree is used for each concurrent implementation.

tickets.title: Provision Linear hierarchy idempotently
tickets.story: As the delivery lead, I can create the complete board without duplicates.
acceptance: Bootstrap creates six epic parents, 42 tickets, labels and two non-overlapping cycles.
Second run creates zero duplicate issues and retains existing human edits.
Ticket dependencies become blocks relations and a readback mapping contains every issue ID.

tickets.title: Link GitHub and Linear; mirror Origin optionally
tickets.story: As the delivery lead, I see authoritative PR progress next to acceptance criteria.
acceptance: Native integration maps opened PR to In Progress, review to In Review, merge to Ready for QA.
A signed Linear change updates only the designated metadata comment when optional bridge is enabled.
Origin mirror, if enabled, leaves GitHub Issues and Actions authoritative.

tickets.title: Lock dependencies and audit upstream surface
tickets.story: As a maintainer, I can explain every runtime dependency.
acceptance: Lockfile resolves FastMCP, psycopg, pgvector and billing dependencies at exact versions.
Dependency licenses and selected public imports are recorded.
No chat frontend, provider router or general agent framework is included; any Redis dependency is justified solely for shared OAuth state, not memory jobs.

tickets.title: Apply PostgreSQL 17 and vector migration
tickets.story: As an operator, I can create the complete schema on a blank database.
acceptance: Migration applies with ON_ERROR_STOP against PostgreSQL 17 and pgvector 0.8.x.
Composite tenant/project foreign keys prevent mismatched parentage.
Vectors have one declared dimension and HNSW cosine opclass with m=16 and ef_construction=64.

tickets.title: Separate database roles and fail-closed RLS
tickets.story: As a tenant, other customers and unauthorized projects cannot read my memory.
acceptance: Runtime role owns no protected tables and has neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS.
Missing or malformed request identity fails closed.
Direct SQL tests deny another tenant and another project within the same tenant.

tickets.title: Define the two typed MCP tool contracts
tickets.story: As a native-client user, my agent discovers unambiguous commit and recall tools.
acceptance: Input and output schemas reject unknown fields and oversized content.
Both tools carry explicit effect/idempotency annotations and compact descriptions.
No tenant ID in client arguments can change authenticated tenant identity.

tickets.title: Serve authenticated Streamable HTTP and hosted-client OAuth
tickets.story: As a user, I can connect a scoped bearer token to the remote endpoint.
acceptance: Initialize, tools/list and tools/call succeed over Streamable HTTP.
Missing, expired, revoked, wrong-project and insufficient-scope tokens are denied.
Origin/Host validation and bounded body handling reject hostile requests.
OAuth uses established FastMCP/provider components with exact issuer, audience/resource, callback allowlist, S256 PKCE and explicit issuer/subject-to-paid-key binding.
Encrypted shared OAuth state survives restart; unlinked identities and guessed project/tenant IDs fail closed.

tickets.title: Make commit_memory atomic and idempotent
tickets.story: As a user, retries never create duplicate decisions or tasks.
acceptance: Same idempotency key and canonical payload returns the stored result.
Same key with a different payload returns a conflict without side effects.
Concurrent duplicate requests yield exactly one persisted event and one embedding job.

tickets.title: Implement exact constraint ledger and revisions
tickets.story: As a project owner, approved constraints survive topic changes.
acceptance: Active constraints are independent of semantic distance and top-k memory count.
Contradictory updates require explicit supersession/revision handling.
A stale revision cannot silently overwrite a newer accepted decision.

tickets.title: Implement durable embedding worker
tickets.story: As an operator, committed memory eventually receives a valid embedding.
acceptance: Database transaction schedules work durably before commit responds.
Worker retries transient provider failures with bounded attempts and visible dead letters.
Crash after a provider response but before acknowledgment does not create duplicate embeddings.

tickets.title: Implement hybrid context procedure
tickets.story: As a user, recall returns exact constraints and relevant semantic memories.
acceptance: match_project_context applies caller project authorization and cosine ranking.
All eligible active constraints are returned or an explicit packet-size error/truncation policy is applied.
Packet includes provenance, version and embedding-pending indicators where applicable.

tickets.title: Run service acceptance and isolation suite
tickets.story: As a release owner, a green build proves memory correctness boundaries.
acceptance: Tests cover scoped credentials, tenant leakage, project leakage, replay and concurrent revisions.
A provider timeout produces a bounded response and durable work state.
No test substitutes the migration-owner role for runtime-role isolation assertions.

tickets.title: Deploy staging with TLS and streaming proxy
tickets.story: As a tester, I reach a stable HTTPS MCP endpoint.
acceptance: Caddy obtains a valid certificate using controlled DNS/ports.
Streaming chunks are delivered promptly without proxy buffering.
Database and application admin ports are inaccessible from the public network.

tickets.title: Add liveness readiness and private diagnostics
tickets.story: As an operator, I distinguish process failure from database dependency failure.
acceptance: Liveness avoids provider/database dependence; readiness verifies required local dependencies.
Readiness contains no database DSN, tenant data or secret values.
An external monitor detects controlled downtime and records recovery.

tickets.title: Ship CI and immutable blue-green release
tickets.story: As a release owner, failed candidates never replace healthy production.
acceptance: CI lints, tests a real vector-enabled Postgres and builds an immutable OCI digest.
Deploy starts inactive color, waits for readiness and runs MCP smoke tests before proxy switch.
Rollback restores previous digest without destructive schema reversal.

tickets.title: Verify Claude supported surfaces
tickets.story: As a Claude user, I can retain and recall a decision in supported app surfaces.
acceptance: Record account plan, client version, transport, auth mode and observation date.
Commit from one tested Claude surface and recall the exact constraint in a separate session.
Document any OAuth, connector permission, confirmation or mobile limitation.
Hosted Claude completes discovery, PKCE login, both tools and token refresh; a mobile claim requires a separate observed mobile test.

tickets.title: Verify ChatGPT MCP and Custom GPT distinction
tickets.story: As a ChatGPT user, onboarding matches the actual supported integration surface.
acceptance: Test MCP connection on an eligible account with permitted read and write tools.
Do not describe a Custom GPT Action as native MCP; separately test the REST adapter if offered.
Record required authorization/confirmation and supported account/client matrix.
Native ChatGPT OAuth discovery, exact callback, S256 PKCE, consent and refresh pass against the deployed provider; personal-key tests alone cannot pass this gate.

tickets.title: Verify Cursor and Claude Code clients
tickets.story: As a developer, I can use memory in my existing coding workflow.
acceptance: Both clients complete initialize, list, commit and recall against staging.
A decision committed in one client is recalled with provenance in the other.
Document exact config and token replacement/revocation procedure.

tickets.title: Create truthful landing and plan definitions
tickets.story: As a buyer, I understand product value, access and usage limits.
acceptance: Starter is $15/month for five projects and personal keys.
Pro/Team is $49/month with unlimited project count and shared organization memory; usage limits remain explicit.
The page states native-client eligibility, data handling and current beta limitations.

tickets.title: Create Stripe catalog and server-side Checkout
tickets.story: As a buyer, I can subscribe to the chosen server-validated plan.
acceptance: Price IDs are created once and looked up from controlled configuration.
Browser cannot set arbitrary price, tenant entitlement or subscription status.
Checkout has verified return-origin handling and an opaque one-use enrollment claim.

tickets.title: Handle Stripe events with durable reconciliation
tickets.story: As a buyer, valid payment provisions my tenant once.
acceptance: Raw-body signature verification rejects forged and stale signatures.
Duplicate and out-of-order events reconcile current subscription status without duplicate tenants.
Only valid allowed products and billable states enable the requested tier.
Concurrent deliveries of the same event and distinct events for one subscription produce one tenant and entitlement result; a lost response followed by retry creates no duplicate key or enrollment.

tickets.title: Issue and reveal scoped access keys once
tickets.story: As an authenticated customer, I receive usable instructions without exposing my key.
acceptance: Raw token is generated with cryptographic entropy; database stores only a keyed digest.
The one-use claim is bound to the checkout owner and cannot be replayed or guessed.
Key page is no-store, no-referrer and has no analytics or third-party scripts.

tickets.title: Provide billing portal and cancellation behavior
tickets.story: As a customer, I can manage billing and understand entitlement expiry.
acceptance: Portal creation verifies customer ownership instead of accepting arbitrary customer IDs.
Cancellation at period end retains access until the authoritative end date.
Failed payment grace, canceled subscription and downgrade over five projects have explicit tested policies.

tickets.title: Implement project access and team memberships
tickets.story: As an organization owner, I can share selected memory without sharing secret keys.
acceptance: Shared organization memory requires explicit membership and project permissions.
Each member uses individually revocable credentials and cannot promote their own role.
Invitation/recovery flow is tested or Team enrollment is explicitly operator-assisted for beta.

tickets.title: Measure realistic multiclient load
tickets.story: As an operator, I know safe concurrency and latency limits.
acceptance: Run mixed commit/recall load for at least 30 minutes using production-sized pools.
Record p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue lag, database saturation and cost at target concurrency.
Admission control responds consistently when measured capacity is exceeded.

tickets.title: Benchmark filtered HNSW recall
tickets.story: As a user, selective projects still return relevant context.
acceptance: Compare approximate top-k with exact cosine on labeled representative project distributions.
Record ef_search and iterative-scan settings with recall@k and latency.
Small/selective-project exact fallback and constraint completeness have explicit acceptance thresholds.

tickets.title: Test token revocation and session boundaries
tickets.story: As a customer, revoking a key stops future use promptly.
acceptance: A revoked credential cannot authorize a new request even with an old MCP session ID.
Concurrent tenants and reused pool connections never exchange authentication context.
Rotation replaces per-client credentials without storing tokens in URL query strings.
An API key expiring during an active MCP session blocks the next tool call; OAuth reference-token expiry refreshes only while the bound key and subscription remain authorized.

tickets.title: Evaluate memory steering and prompt injection
tickets.story: As a user, memory improves continuity without treating recalled data as instructions.
acceptance: Twenty scripted conversations test recall-before-work and commit-after-approved-outcome behavior.
Malicious memory asking for exfiltration or instruction override is treated as data.
Measure missed writes, duplicate writes, incorrect constraints and confirmation friction per client.

tickets.title: Exercise backup restore and incident runbook
tickets.story: As an operator, I can recover data on an independent database.
acceptance: Restore a backup into a fresh environment and verify counts plus cross-tenant isolation.
Record measured RPO/RTO and confirm application role grants survived restore.
Drill credential compromise, provider outage and failed deploy with named response owner.
Restore into a new disposable database, run a real MCP commit/recall and runtime-role isolation checks there, and reapply post-backup deletion/revocation records before any traffic cutover.

tickets.title: Run full commercial lifecycle tests
tickets.story: As a release owner, billing and access stay consistent through lifecycle events.
acceptance: Stripe test-mode checkout yields one tenant and a working scoped key.
Replay webhook, refund/cancel/downgrade and delayed-payment cases match policy.
Quota enforcement prevents Starter project six and unauthorized Team sharing.

tickets.title: Recruit ten eligible design partners
tickets.story: As a commercial lead, I find users with repeated multi-model project work.
acceptance: Recruit from permission-appropriate X, Reddit and developer Discord participation.
Every invitation discloses beta status, supported native clients and paid plan terms.
Ten candidates have an ICP fit, supported account, consent and onboarding slot.

tickets.title: Run supervised beta activation
tickets.story: As a beta customer, I get a visible cross-client memory win quickly.
acceptance: At least five users complete checkout/key connection/commit/recall sequence.
Measure time to first cross-client recall and log every blocking step.
No customer token or unredacted private memory enters issue trackers or recordings.

tickets.title: Complete privacy export deletion and support readiness
tickets.story: As a customer, I can control my saved memory and reach support.
acceptance: Privacy notice states stored fields, embedding processor, retention and deletion behavior.
Export and deletion are exercised on a test tenant, including queued work and backup retention explanation.
Support contact, response window and security reporting path are published.

tickets.title: Triage beta friction and gate public launch
tickets.story: As a release owner, I launch only when customer-critical behavior passes.
acceptance: No open tenant leakage, lost writes, billing duplication or unusable onboarding defects remain.
Publish measured compatibility matrix and remove unverified client claims.
Owner signs launch decision with rollback criteria, measured capacity and remaining limitations.

tickets.title: Publish reproducible native-workflow demo
tickets.story: As a prospective customer, I can see a specific cross-model continuity benefit.
acceptance: Demo commits a technical decision in one native client and recalls it in another.
Shows setup, latency, provenance and limitations using synthetic data.
Landing CTA points to working paid checkout with accurate plan limits.

tickets.title: Launch Product Hunt and Show HN submissions
tickets.story: As a founder, I invite trial from appropriate developer communities.
acceptance: Submissions use factual product claims and disclose maker affiliation.
Show HN provides a usable demonstration and links to implementation/behavior explanations.
Product Hunt launch assets and support coverage are ready before publishing.

tickets.title: Monitor first live purchases and capacity
tickets.story: As the on-call owner, I verify money turns into working product access.
acceptance: A legitimate live purchase reaches expected entitlement and successful native recall.
Alert on failed webhook processing, entitlement mismatch, error rate and work-queue lag.
Track gross MRR, Stripe fees, provider costs and support time separately.

tickets.title: Record launch outcome and next-week priorities
tickets.story: As the founder, I prioritize based on activation and paid behavior.
acceptance: Report eligible visitors, checkout starts, paid conversions and activated users.
Collect at least three user descriptions of the actual memory problem solved.
Freeze unsupported expansion until activation failures and reliability debt are ranked.

tickets.title: Close highest-impact production follow-ups
tickets.story: As a customer, first-week bugs receive measured fixes.
acceptance: All launch P1/P2 incidents have owners, reproduction and correction evidence.
Retest outage recovery and cost limits using observed real traffic shapes.
Review error budget and whether managed redundancy is now justified.

tickets.title: Measure retention and decide expansion
tickets.story: As a founder, I know whether users repeatedly need shared memory.
acceptance: Report seven-day retained activated users and repeat cross-client recall rate.
Interview churned or inactive customers before adding more integrations.
Decide pricing, quotas and next client investment from measured adoption and margin.
